description: Global execution contracts, workspace discipline, evidence rules, and anti-lazy operating rails for the v5 super operator.
notes: Rebuild and _old-surface preservation are intentionally excluded from skill catalogs and belong to the direct super-prompt phase flow.
These skills define how the operator must behave while applying analysis, world, visual, media, and QA skills.

skills.title: Protect mechanic truth
skills.intent: Keep controls, loop semantics, collisions, scoring, win/loss logic, timing, and actionability protected unless a tiny repair is clearly necessary.
required_actions: Treat the current gameplay reality as protected evidence.
Prefer cosmetic, semantic, HUD, asset, layout, and procedural-art changes over mechanic rewrites.
If a proposed change risks playability, mark it unsafe and route around it.
acceptance_bar: The remixed result remains mechanically truthful to the source game.
No skill execution invents new ungrounded mechanics.
failure_modes_prevented: Theme fantasy overriding real game behavior
Visual changes breaking controls or collision expectations

skills.title: Stay mobile-first and runtime-disciplined
skills.intent: Preserve the mobile-first operational posture across all phases, including runtime validation and screenshot capture.
required_actions: Assume the primary validation target is a mobile portrait viewport.
Keep controls reachable, CTA paths visible, and overlays non-blocking.
Use the assigned validation/runtime channel only when browser-grounded evidence is needed.
acceptance_bar: The remixed game is actionable on mobile.
Validation evidence comes from the assigned runtime rather than assumptions.

skills.title: Treat catalogs as read-only authority
skills.intent: Use `catalogs/` as reference input rather than authored output.
required_actions: Read `catalogs/skills/` as capability rails.
Read media catalogs as approved asset authority when applicable.
Write generated artifacts outside `catalogs/`.
acceptance_bar: No operator step mutates catalog files.
Generated work is written into normal workspace surfaces and artifacts.
failure_modes_prevented: Operators treating reference catalogs as editable output
Losing separation between authority inputs and generated deliverables

skills.title: Produce real artifacts and real evidence
skills.intent: Require concrete files, screenshots, and contracts instead of hand-wavy summaries.
required_actions: Write required planning and validation artifacts when the phase calls for them.
Use real screenshots instead of descriptive substitutes when evidence is required.
Keep contract outputs aligned with the actual work performed.
acceptance_bar: Evidence artifacts are real, current, and phase-appropriate.
The super operator leaves an auditable trail of what was decided and validated.

skills.title: Use `_trash` as the single explicit deletion lifecycle
skills.intent: Standardize all intentionally deletable surfaces under one deterministic naming contract that runtime cleanup can enforce before workspace promotion.
required_actions: Mark obsolete or intentionally deletable files with the `_trash` suffix before extension (for example: `index_trash.html`, `game_trash.js`, `screen_intro_trash.png`).
Mark obsolete or intentionally deletable directories with the `_trash` suffix (for example: `assets_trash/`).
Apply the same `_trash` convention to original/baseline screenshots when they are not meant to survive as final evidence artifacts.
Do not use parallel delete markers like `_old` or ad-hoc names for explicitly deletable surfaces.
acceptance_bar: Explicitly deletable surfaces are consistently named with `_trash`.
No ambiguous stale artifacts remain due to mixed deletion naming conventions.
failure_modes_prevented: Obsolete files accidentally promoted as canonical output
Baseline screenshot clutter surviving due to naming drift

skills.title: Do not collapse into a lazy mega-prompt
skills.intent: Force the operator to execute in explicit phases with explicit obligations instead of vague all-at-once creativity.
required_actions: Follow a clear phase order across analysis, worlding, visuals, media, and QA.
Use sub-artifacts and subgrouped skills instead of opaque creative drift.
Make decisions explainable in terms of source truth and skill contracts.
acceptance_bar: The operator can explain why each transformation happened.
The final prompt remains inspectable rather than magical.
failure_modes_prevented: Dropping important rails from merged source prompts
Unstructured creativity that cannot be debugged

skills.title: Keep all phases aligned
skills.intent: Ensure analysis, world, visual, media, and QA outputs describe the same remixed game.
required_actions: Keep terminology stable across artifacts and UI copy.
Ensure world, progression, and visual evolution agree with the same premise.
Use QA findings to repair contradictions rather than papering over them.
acceptance_bar: Blueprint, worlding, visuals, media choices, and QA describe one coherent target.
No phase implies mechanics or states unsupported by the others.
